rationale: The Adobe-C++ functionobjects benchmark is a timing benchmark built from heavily templated C++: many small, arithmetic-intensive functor/template functions executing in hot loops, with essentially no static profile available to identify cold code. Because execution time is concentrated in these small hot functions, I weight SUB most aggressively (high tolerance on runtime/size cost, high security gain) since arithmetic substitution yields strong obfuscation per unit of overhead and composes well with inlined template code, and SPLIT as a near-free complement that increases basic-block fragmentation for later passes. FLA and BCF get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights but deliberately low runtime tolerance, so the feature-driven selector applies them only to functions whose features indicate sufficient gain relative to cost (e.g., larger or branch-heavy dispatch loops rather than tight inner arithmetic loops), which is where flattening actually pays off. IBR and ICALL receive moderate weights: indirect branches and calls add meaningful disassembly/decompilation resistance at acceptable cost, and they synergize with the code's existing functor-style indirection, while IGV is kept moderate since this benchmark has few globals, limiting both its benefit and its risk. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept at or above 0.6 everywhere (highest for the structurally simplest passes) to bias the selector away from transforming fragile constructs like exception-handling or landing-pad blocks common in C++ code, preserving correctness.
